Our curriculum is designed on the premise that, for students to flourish, they need to acquire and remember knowledge incrementally over time. Once this core knowledge is firmly secured in their long-term memory, they can apply it to each subject and beyond.
Our curriculum is the key lever in addressing social disadvantage; in levelling the playing field between those with social and economic advantages and those without.
Those with a rich and wide knowledge are advantaged. Those without are dependent on those that do. We need to ensure that all London Academy students are equipped with a powerful academic knowledge to liberate them in their life ahead.
London Academy students also need the social, emotional, moral, cultural, spiritual and entrepreneurial development that empowers them to become whoever they choose to be. How does our curriculum achieve this? Through three core elements:

Our curriculum is designed on the premise that, for students to flourish, they need to acquire and remember knowledge incrementally over time. Once this core knowledge is firmly secured in their long-term memory, they can apply it to each subject and beyond.
Our curriculum is the key lever in addressing social disadvantage; in levelling the playing field between those with social and economic advantages and those without.

London Academy students also need the social, emotional, moral, cultural, spiritual and entrepreneurial development that empowers them to become whoever they choose to be. How does our curriculum achieve this? Through three core elements:

Our curriculum is designed on the premise that, for students to flourish, they need to acquire and remember knowledge incrementally over time. Once this core knowledge is firmly secured in their long-term memory, they can apply it to each subject and beyond.
Our curriculum is the key lever in addressing social disadvantage; in levelling the playing field between those with social and economic advantages and those without.
Those with a rich and wide knowledge are advantaged. Those without are dependent on those that do. We need to ensure that all London Academy students are equipped with a powerful academic knowledge to liberate them in their life ahead.
London Academy students also need the social, emotional, moral, cultural, spiritual and entrepreneurial development that empowers them to become whoever they choose to be. How does our curriculum achieve this? Through three core elements:

Career Ready
Career Ready is a national social mobility charity running a programme for students studying either Business, ICT, Maths or Economics, to improve their employability skills.
Running from January (Year 12) to January (Year 13), each participant benefits from a range of in-house masterclasses, trips to organisations, an individual business mentor, and the chance to complete a 4–6-week paid internship during the summer holidays.
Previous internships and visits include Morgan Stanley, EY, BUPA, Citi, Savills and CBRE.
To qualify for this valuable scheme, students require the right to work in the UK and be available during the summer holidays.
More information: www.careerready.org.uk

Careers
Our careers education
The comprehensive careers programme at London Academy includes:
– careers education sessions – careers guidance activities (group work and individual interviews) – information and research activities – work-related learning
In addition, specific careers lessons form part of the academy’s PSHE programme and subject curriculum.
How we deliver the programme
• The PSHE curriculum via specific form time lessons (12 lessons per year) • Careers interviews with an independent careers advisor – all students have a careers interview during KS4 & KS5 • The annual London Academy Careers Fair hosting over 100 professional exhibitors from a wide range of sectors • A dedicated UCAS mentor for all Year 12 & Year 13 students • University visits as part of our LA7 commitment to students.
• Work experience opportunities for students in KS4 & KS5
How we measure impact
The success of our students in securing academic outcomes and their next destinations highlight the impact of our careers provision:
View our latest weekly careers newsletter
London Academy hass partnerships with the following organisations to support our careers guidance delivery: Access Inspiration, eClips, iCould, START, Careers Box, and The Careers People.
Skillsometer
Designed for those unsure of what careers jobs they may be interested in, Skillsometer is a quiz that enables pupils to think more clearly about their skills and interests. By reflecting on several statements (presented within six occupational categories: Artistic, Realistic, Investigative, Conventional, Enterprising, and Social), to categorise what they love, are not sure about, or dislike, this can be a helpful first step in identifying possible future jobs.
Once users complete the quiz, they’re offered a short list of job suggestions to best suit their particular skills and interests. Each job can then be explored through a description with information on pay and hours. For further information on the job, and to compare with other jobs, the user could then progress to the Careerometer.
Careerometer
Careerometer offers easy access to labour market information. Users can search for different careers and find out more about wages and projected growth within that industry. It’s a great way for students to explore potential careers.

Destinations
Sixth Form Destinations
We help our students make the best decisions about their next steps.
Careers and university are a key focus of our form time programme in Years 12 and 13, and students receive informed support from form tutors and in-school careers advisors on choosing their pathways and completing applications.
More than 90% of London Academy students choose to attend university, with more than 50% typically receiving offers from the leading Russell Group universities each year. An increasing number also explore high-quality degree apprenticeships, applying for schemes with leading companies in fields such as finance, consultancy, and engineering.
Students targeting Oxbridge and medicine/dentistry/law courses receive dedicated guidance and support, focused on preparation for the admissions tests and interviews. In 2022-23, three of our students successfully secured places – and are now studying – at Oxford or Cambridge.
